raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With DP attention every scheduler step exchanges one small `MLPSyncBatchInfo` row per attention rank on the CPU gloo group (token counts, attention pairs, the CUDA-graph votes, the forward mode). gloo implements `all_gather` as a ring of `world_size - 1` serial hops, so the latency of that exchange grows linearly with the attention world. A gather onto group rank 0 followed by a broadcast is one hop plus a log-depth tree and fills the same buffer.

## Modifications

- `exchange_sync_rows` in `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py` fills the flat buffer in group-rank order exactly like `all_gather_single`. On a CPU group with more than two ranks it gathers every rank's row onto group rank 0 (directly into the row views of the output) and broadcasts the filled buffer; device tensors and two-rank groups keep `all_gather_single`, since at two ranks the ring is already the single hop.
- `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather` calls it on its all-gather path; the existing `use_all_reduce` branch is unchanged.
- Tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_dp_attn.py`): the two existing mocks of `all_gather_single` move to the new seam. `TestSyncRowExchangeGloo` spawns an 8-rank gloo world and, for sub-groups of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 ranks over four rounds with a random per-rank sleep and busy-wait before each exchange, asserts that the exchange matches the ring all-gather bitwise on every rank and that the real `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather` still produces the right `global_num_tokens`, `global_attention_pairs` and decode CUDA-graph vote. The world is capped at 8 because every rank is a spawned interpreter and the hosted CPU runner's memory bounds it; the file's `est_time` is raised accordingly.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the exchanged rows are bitwise identical to the all-gather result, which the new test checks on every rank.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark is included. The change swaps a ring all-gather for gather + broadcast on CPU groups larger than two ranks, and the new test checks the exchanged rows are identical; two-rank groups and device tensors keep the previous path.

Local validation on this head: `python3 test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_dp_attn.py` passes all 18 tests. `isort`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, `codespell`, `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py` at the pinned pre-commit versions report nothing.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -55,6 +55,30 @@
 _ENABLE_METRICS_DP_ATTENTION = envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DP_ATTENTION.get()
 
 
+def exchange_sync_rows(
+    global_flat: torch.Tensor,
+    local_row: torch.Tensor,
+    group: torch.distributed.ProcessGroup,
+) -> None:
+    """Fill ``global_flat`` with every rank's ``local_row`` in group-rank order,
+    like ``all_gather_single``. On gloo the all-gather is a ring of world_size - 1
+    serial hops; gather + broadcast is one hop plus a log-depth tree. At two
+    ranks the ring is the single hop, so it stays."""
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size(group)
+    if local_row.device.type != "cpu" or world_size <= 2:
+        all_gather_single(global_flat, local_row, group=group)
+        return
+    root = torch.distributed.get_global_rank(group, 0)
+    rows = global_flat.view(world_size, local_row.numel())
+    if torch.distributed.get_rank(group) == 0:
+        torch.distributed.gather(
+            local_row, gather_list=list(rows.unbind(0)), dst=root, group=group
+        )
+    else:
+        torch.distributed.gather(local_row, dst=root, group=group)
+    torch.distributed.broadcast(global_flat, src=root, group=group)
+
+

 ) -> bool:

+# The ring path (2), primes, an even non-power-of-two, and two powers of two
+# with different gather / broadcast tree depths. Every rank is a spawned
+# interpreter, so the hosted CPU runner's memory caps the largest world.
+_EXCHANGE_WORLDS = (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8)
+_EXCHANGE_ROUNDS = 4
+
+
+def _exchange_worker(rank, world, port, out_q):
+    """One gloo rank: every sub-world below runs the one-hop exchange and the
+    real `MLPSyncBatchInfo.all_gather` for several rounds, each rank arriving
+    after a random delay and a random amount of preceding CPU work."""
+    import random
+
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        "gloo",
+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=world,
+        timeout=datetime.timedelta(seconds=60),
+    )
+    try:
+        for sub in _EXCHANGE_WORLDS:
+            group = dist.new_group(list(range(sub)))
+            if rank >= sub:
+                continue
+            rng = random.Random(1000 * sub + rank)
+            for round_idx in range(_EXCHANGE_ROUNDS):
+                info = dp_attn.MLPSyncBatchInfo(
+                    num_dp_ranks=sub,
+                    tp_size=1,
+                    cp_size=1,
+                    num_tokens=3 + rank + 100 * round_idx,
+                    num_tokens_for_logprob=3 + rank,
+                    can_run_decode_cuda_graph=rank != round_idx % sub,
+                    can_run_draft_cuda_graph=True,
+                    can_run_prefill_cuda_graph=True,
+                    is_extend_in_batch=False,
+                    local_can_run_tbo=False,
+                    local_forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE.value,
+                    attention_pairs=1000 * (rank + 1) + round_idx,
+                )
+                local = info._get_local_tensor(device="cpu")
+                reference = torch.zeros(sub * local.numel(), dtype=torch.int64)
+                dp_attn.all_gather_single(reference, local, group=group)
+                # Skewed arrival: a random sleep plus preceding work of a
+                # random length (tens of microseconds to ~100 ms).
+                time.sleep(rng.uniform(0.0, 0.05))
+                busy_until = time.perf_counter() + rng.uniform(0.0, 0.05)
+                while time.perf_counter() < busy_until:
+                    pass
+                exchanged = torch.zeros_like(reference)
+                dp_attn.exchange_sync_rows(exchanged, local, group=group)
+                parallel = SimpleNamespace(
+                    tp_group=SimpleNamespace(
+                        active_ranks_cpu=torch.ones(sub, dtype=torch.int64)
+                    )
+                )
+                with patch.object(dp_attn, "get_parallel", return_value=parallel):
+                    info.all_gather(device="cpu", group=group)
+                out_q.put(
+                    (
+                        sub,
+                        round_idx,
+                        rank,
+                        torch.equal(exchanged, reference),
+                        info.global_num_tokens,
+                        info.global_attention_pairs,
+                        info.can_run_decode_cuda_graph,
+                    )
+                )
+    finally:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+class TestSyncRowExchangeGloo(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_one_hop_exchange_matches_all_gather_on_every_rank(self):
+        """The gloo exchange agrees bitwise with the ring all-gather on every
+        rank of worlds 2..8 (primes, an even non-power-of-two, powers of two),
+        over several rounds with random per-rank arrival skew."""
+        world = max(_EXCHANGE_WORLDS)
+        sock = socket.socket()
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+        sock.close()
+        ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+        out_q = ctx.Queue()
+        procs = [
+            ctx.Process(target=_exchange_worker, args=(r, world, port, out_q))
+            for r in range(world)
+        ]
+        results = {}
+        try:
+            for proc in procs:
+                proc.start()
+            for _ in range(sum(_EXCHANGE_WORLDS) * _EXCHANGE_ROUNDS):
+                sub, round_idx, rank, same, tokens, pairs, graph = out_q.get(
+                    timeout=240
+                )
+                results[(sub, round_idx, rank)] = (same, tokens, pairs, graph)
+            for proc in procs:
+                proc.join(timeout=60)
+                self.assertEqual(proc.exitcode, 0)
+        finally:
+            # An init-phase death must not park the shard on the gloo timeout.
+            for proc in procs:
+                if proc.is_alive():
+                    proc.kill()
+                    proc.join(timeout=10)
+        for sub in _EXCHANGE_WORLDS:
+            for round_idx in range(_EXCHANGE_ROUNDS):
+                for rank in range(sub):
+                    same, tokens, pairs, graph = results[(sub, round_idx, rank)]
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        same, f"world {sub} round {round_idx} rank {rank} differs"
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        tokens, [3 + r + 100 * round_idx for r in range(sub)]
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        pairs, [1000 * (r + 1) + round_idx for r in range(sub)]
+                    )
+                    # One rank votes eager each round; the min reaches every rank.
+                    self.assertFalse(graph)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
